title: Nonlinear Functions, Part 3: Traps and the Fast Way

beats.say: In this video, we look at five mistakes students make with nonlinear functions, and then use Desmos to find a vertex and zeros, and to find when an exponential reaches a value.
Each trap is shown as a wrong line first, then the right line, with the reason it's so tempting.
Trap one. A machine loses twenty percent of its value each year. Students use the percent itself as the factor, instead of what's left after the loss.
beats.wrong_why: 0.2 is the loss, not what remains

beats.say: Losing twenty percent leaves eighty percent, so the factor is zero point eight. Likewise, a three percent increase has a factor of one point zero three.

scenes.title: Trap 2: the sign in vertex form

beats.say: Trap two. In vertex form, the number inside the parentheses has the opposite sign to the x coordinate of the vertex. Students read it as it appears.
The factor x plus three is x minus negative three. So h is negative three, and the vertex is negative three comma negative seven.
Trap three. For f of x equals two x squared, find f of negative two. Without parentheses, students square only the two and keep the negative sign outside.
Negative two, squared, is positive four, because a negative times a negative is positive. Then two times four is eight.
Trap four. The vertex is the turning point of the parabola, and the zeros are where it crosses the x axis. A question about zeros isn't asking for the vertex.
beats.wrong_why: The vertex is not a zero here

beats.say: For negative x squared plus six x minus five, the zeros are one and five, and the vertex is at three comma four.
beats.right_why: Where the graph crosses the x-axis

beats.say: Trap five. If a quantity doubles every five hours, the exponent is t divided by five. Students multiply by five instead, which makes the quantity double five times as fast.
After five hours, t over five is one, so the quantity doubles once. That's the correct pace.
beats.right_why: t divided by the doubling time

beats.say: Desmos is strong on this skill. Graph the function and click the grey dots, and the vertex, the zeros, and the y-intercept are all marked for you.
Open a fresh graph, and type the function from our easy example.
Type y equals negative x, the caret key and a two, the right arrow, then plus six x minus five.
Click the top of the parabola, and then click its grey dot. Desmos shows three comma four, the vertex.
Now click the two grey dots on the x axis. The zeros are x equals one and x equals five.

scenes.title: When does it reach a value?

beats.say: Desmos also tells us when an exponential reaches a value. For the machine, graph the value function and the line y equals twenty thousand, and find where they meet.
We graph the exponential decay and the horizontal line, and click where they cross.
Type y equals forty-five thousand times zero point eight, then the caret key and an x. Press the right arrow after the exponent.
Type y equals twenty thousand. This horizontal line is the value we want the machine to fall below.
Click the crossing point. The x value is about three point six three. So the value reaches twenty thousand partway through the fourth year, which is why the answer is four whole years.
Now a practice problem. Find the vertex of f of x equals x squared minus four x minus five. Pause the video, try it, and then watch the solution.
The x coordinate of the vertex is negative b over two a. Here b is negative four and a is one.
Two times one is two. Negative four over two is negative two, and the minus sign in front makes it positive two.
To find the y coordinate, evaluate the function at x equals two.
Two squared is four, and four times two is eight, so the first two terms are four and negative eight.
Four minus eight minus five is negative nine. So the vertex is two comma negative nine, and it's a minimum, because a is positive.
Check with the zeros. The function factors as x minus five, times x plus one, so the zeros are five and negative one. Halfway between them is two, which matches the vertex.
To recap. Use the remaining fraction as the factor for decay, reverse the sign inside vertex form, and square negative inputs in parentheses.
The vertex is the turning point, and zeros are x-intercepts. For doubling times, divide t by the doubling time.
beats.item: Vertex is not a zero; divide by d

beats.say: Use Desmos for vertices, zeros, and when an exponential reaches a value. In the next unit, we study Problem-Solving and Data Analysis, starting with ratios and rates.
